title: Story 04: Single Agent Task — Minimal Breakdown
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Polish the Login Page Button Styles ## Analysis **Request:** "Polish the login page button styles" **Key observations:** 1. The login page is **already built and functional** — this is visual polish, not new functionality. 2. This is a **Webapp sub-team** task — it's about the UI/presentation layer. 3. The correct phase flow is **Styling: Plan → Style → Validate** — two separate tasks to the same styler (Plan + Style), plus a validation task. 4. This is a **chore** — maintenance/polish on existing UI with no new user-facing capability. The buttons already work; we're only improving their appearance. **Issue hierarchy:** ``` CHORE: "Polish login page button styles" (tag: chore, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress) ├── Task "Plan button style polish" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-styler, status: todo) ├── Task "Style login page buttons" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-styler, status: todo) ← blocked by Plan └── Task "Validate button style polish" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-validator, status: todo) ← blocked by Style ``` **Why this structure:** - One deliverable (the chore) with 3 phase tasks → a parent is justified (groups 2+ related issues). - Styling flow: Plan + Style go to the **same styler** as two **separate** tasks (never collapse phases), and Validate goes to the **validator** (never the styler who did the work). - No developer needed — the login page already exists and only visual changes are required. - No gate tracker needed — this is single-team work with no provider/consumer relationship. - No completion/verification child — the status loop completes the parent. --- ## Commands (in execution order) ### Step 1 — Create the parent chore ```bash agt create "Polish login page button styles" \ --tags chore \ --assignee project-manager \ --status todo ``` **Reasoning:** This is visual polish/maintenance on an existing UI element — no new user-facing capability is being added, so `chore` is the correct structural tag. The parent is assigned to me (PM) and starts at `todo`. I'll capture the returned ID as `

`. --- ### Step 2 — Create Phase 1: Plan (styler) ```bash agt create "Plan button style polish" \ --tags task \ --assignee webapp-styler \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** The Styling phase flow starts with Plan. Even for a small styling task, the styler plans their approach (which buttons, what visual changes, spacing, colors, hover states, etc.). One task per phase — never skip planning. Assigned to `webapp-styler` (the same agent who will do the styling). I'll capture this ID as ``. --- ### Step 3 — Create Phase 2: Style (styler) ```bash agt create "Style login page buttons" \ --tags task \ --assignee webapp-styler \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** The second phase of the Styling flow. Same styler does the actual visual polish work. This is a **separate task** from Plan — the skill explicitly requires one task per phase even when the same agent does both. I'll capture this ID as ``. --- ### Step 4 — Create Phase 3: Validate (validator) ```bash agt create "Validate button style polish" \ --tags task \ --assignee webapp-validator \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Validation is **always** a separate task assigned to the team's validator — the styler never validates their own work. For the webapp, this means visual QA, checking button states (default, hover, active, disabled), cross-browser appearance, and any E2E checks. I'll capture this ID as ``. --- ### Step 5 — Create blockage: Style blocked by Plan ```bash agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The styler cannot implement the polish before they've planned it. This sequences the work: when Plan (``) is marked `done`, this blockage auto-clears and the work loop picks up the Style task. --- ### Step 6 — Create blockage: Validate blocked by Style ```bash agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The validator cannot validate work that hasn't been done yet. When Style (``) is marked `done`, this blockage auto-clears and validation can begin. --- ### Step 7 — Flip the parent to `in-progress` ```bash agt update

--status in-progress ``` **Reasoning:** The parent must be set to `in-progress` **immediately** after creating its children — never left at `todo`. This signals that work is actively underway. The status loop will complete this parent (→ `closed` + close descendants, since it has no parent) once all three children are `done`. --- ## What happens next (no PM action needed) 1. **Work loop** picks up `` (Plan) — it's `todo`, assigned to `webapp-styler`, has no open blockages. The styler sets it `in-progress`, plans the visual changes, adds a comment with results, marks it `done`. 2. **Auto-clear:** `` done → blockage on `` resolves automatically. 3. **Work loop** picks up `` (Style) — styler implements the polish, comments, marks `done`. 4. **Auto-clear:** `` done → blockage on `` resolves automatically. 5. **Work loop** picks up `` (Validate) — `webapp-validator` tests the visual changes, comments, marks `done`. 6. **Status loop** finds `

` `in-progress` with all children `done` → marks `

` `closed` and closes all three children. Work is fully delivered and cleared from the tracker. **No completion child, no verification task, no manual blockage resolution** — the system handles all of it. --- ## Summary of all commands in order ```bash # 1. Create parent chore agt create "Polish login page button styles" --tags chore --assignee project-manager --status todo # 2. Create Plan task (styler) agt create "Plan button style polish" --tags task --assignee webapp-styler --status todo --parentId

# 3. Create Style task (styler) agt create "Style login page buttons" --tags task --assignee webapp-styler --status todo --parentId

# 4. Create Validate task (validator) agt create "Validate button style polish" --tags task --assignee webapp-validator --status todo --parentId

# 5. Block Style by Plan agt blockages add --by # 6. Block Validate by Style agt blockages add --by # 7. Flip parent to in-progress (LAST) agt update

--status in-progress ```
feedback: Strong response with correct structure, assignments, dependencies, sync pattern (no verify child, parent to in-progress), and status management. The styler-does-plan+style, validator-does-validate split and phase adaptation (no release/dev) are all correct. The one notable miss: used a 'chore' tag where the expected output specifies 'feature' — the agent's reasoning for chore is defensible but does not match the expected tag, slightly lowering hierarchy and behavioralAccuracy.
